title: Soft skills and active listening
lead: The people skills hospitality runs on, and how to make a guest feel heard.

sections.name: Core soft skills
know: Eq understand, respect and anticipate guest needs.
Calm and professional when plans change.
Teamwork keeps every day running smoothly.

rows.name: Emotional intelligence (EQ) and empathy
rows.meta: Understand, respect and anticipate guest needs while keeping a welcoming environment.

rows.name: Active listening and clear communication
rows.meta: Convey information clearly and make sure guests feel heard, which prevents misunderstandings.

rows.name: Conflict resolution and troubleshooting
rows.meta: Manage difficult situations and complaints diplomatically, turning negative experiences into positive ones.

rows.name: Adaptability and resilience
rows.meta: Thrive under pressure, calm and professional when schedules or circumstances change.

rows.name: Teamwork
rows.meta: Work with diverse teams so day-to-day operations run smoothly.

rows.name: Cultural awareness
rows.meta: Respect customs, dining and drinking etiquette, and gestures, for a local and global clientele.

sections.name: Active listening
know: Open body language: arms uncrossed, eye contact, a nod.
No interrupting let them finish before you answer.
Mirror repeat back the core of what they need.

keyPoints.line: understand, respect and anticipate guest needs.

read.where: Delivering exceptional hospitality takes a set of **emotional and interpersonal skills**.

keyPoints.line: body language: arms uncrossed, eye contact, a nod.
let them finish before you answer.
repeat back the core of what they need.

read.where: Active listening transforms standard service into a **memorable experience** by showing guests that we care about their **specific preferences**.

stops.name: The 80/20 rule
stops.text: **Listen 80%** of the time and **speak 20%**, to clarify or offer solutions.

stops.name: Non-verbal cues
stops.text: Keep **open body language** (arms uncrossed), make **direct eye contact** and **nod** to show you’re engaged.

stops.name: No interruptions
stops.text: Let the guest **fully finish speaking** before you offer a resolution or a response.

stops.name: Mirror and paraphrase
stops.text: Repeat back the **core of the guest’s need**: “Just to confirm, you’d like your Old Fashioned to have 3 cherries?”

read.sayIt: Just to make sure we get this right, you would prefer the dressing on the side?

sources: Baldwin Restaurant Group, Hospitality 101 Training (2026), page 3: Core soft skills and active listening.

cards.q: Which soft skill means understanding, respecting and anticipating guest needs?
Clear communication makes guests feel heard. What does it prevent?

cards.answer: Customs, dining and drinking etiquette, and gestures

cards.q: Good conflict resolution turns a negative experience into…
wrong: A note for the manager only
Spend 80% of your time at your tables

cards.q: Which shows a guest you’re engaged, without words?
cards.answer: Arms uncrossed, direct eye contact and a nod
wrong: Arms crossed and a slight lean

cards.q: A guest wants the dressing on the side. Mirroring sounds like…
cards.answer: “Just to make sure we get this right, you would prefer the dressing on the side?”

cards.q: When do you offer a resolution or a response?
cards.answer: After the guest has fully finished speaking
wrong: As soon as you know the answer
